differences.title: 1. EXECUTION CONTEXT
differences.leftDesc: eBPF runs in a sandboxed virtual machine within the kernel, preventing crashes and ensuring security through rigorous safety checks before execution.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules run directly in kernel space, offering powerful but risky access. A bug can easily destabilize the entire operating system.

differences.title: 2. SECURITY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: eBPF programs undergo a verifier phase that statically analyzes code for safety, guaranteeing termination and memory safety before loading into the kernel.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules are loaded with full root privileges. The kernel trusts them implicitly, making security vulnerabilities a major concern.

differences.title: 3. DEVELOPMENT EFFORT
differences.leftDesc: eBPF development allows for quicker iteration cycles and easier debugging within a managed environment, often using higher-level languages and frameworks.
differences.rightDesc: Developing kernel modules involves complex build systems, kernel headers, and deep understanding of kernel internals, leading to longer development times.

differences.title: 4. PROGRAM LIFETIME
differences.leftDesc: eBPF programs are event-driven and can be attached dynamically to specific kernel probes and detached without rebooting the system.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules are loaded into the kernel and remain resident until explicitly unloaded or the system is restarted, posing a higher risk.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE OVERHEAD
differences.leftDesc: Compiled eBPF bytecode runs efficiently with low overhead, often comparable to native code, due to just-in-time compilation and optimized execution.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules have direct access but can introduce performance bottlenecks if not carefully optimized, potentially impacting system responsiveness.

differences.title: 6. VERSATILITY
differences.leftDesc: eBPF excels in network monitoring, security policy enforcement, and application performance analysis by observing kernel and user-space events.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules can modify core kernel behavior, implement entirely new subsystems, or provide hardware drivers, offering broad system control.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: eBPF has a vibrant, rapidly expanding ecosystem with active development in tracing, networking, and security tools across major cloud providers.
differences.rightDesc: Kernel modules have a long history and vast codebase, but innovation pace is slower, and tooling can be fragmented and dated.
